newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares sink ahead of options expiries.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares sink ahead of options expiries.

text.p: Dutch shares closed 1.23 percent lower on Thursday, with a four-day sequence of record high closings coming to an emphatic halt as institutions took profits ahead of Friday's options expiries.

The AEX closed 11.88 points down at 953.37, over 25 points below an all-time high of 978.87 reached at the beginning of the session. Dealers said the early rise reflected a big Wall Street gain and short covering related to bearish options positions.
"With the expiries coming up I think we could see the same sort of volatility tomorrow," said a dealer. "But I don't really believe that this is the end of the bull market."
"People are selling calls in the options market and taking profits," said another dealer, also anticipating hectic conditions in the options market on Friday.

Options trading has been boosted by the booming Dutch share market -- up 47 percent since the beginning of 1997 -- with some 850,000 open interest option contracts recorded on Wednesday afternoon, the Amsterdam bourse said.

The busiest expiration ever for the exchange was in January this year when 411,000 contracts were settled. The exchange estimates its maximum daily processing capacity at more than 500,000 contracts per day.

Dealers said they saw signs that some options players had been betting on an AEX setback, taking short positions in the options market which they had had to cover in the cash market, driving up prices at the beginning of Thursday's session.
Wall Street's overnight drive above 8,000 for the first time and a firm bond market also added to early impetus.

But selling from institutions gathered pace after Wall Street backtracked at its Thursday opening. "When we got up to the new high, we saw some serious institutional selling coming in," said another dealer, adding chart analysts might prove wary about today's trading formations.
